thread:
sam_ae: Urgent — Acme POC is blocked. They're seeing intermittent 500s and apparent rate-limit headers on the dedicated endpoint (redwood-peak-v2, us-west-2). Customer asked for immediate swarming. Request ID from customer: abc123. Can @maria_se or @ryan_infra triage?

maria_se: On it. Can you paste a curl sample + the error snippet from their logs? :eyes:

sam_ae: Here's the request they sent and the response they got:
```curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-peak-v2","input":"long chat history...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
And log excerpt:
```
[2025-11-12T14:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 status=500 error="internal server error" route=/v1/generate
[2025-11-12T14:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 headers="X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0; X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 24"
[2025-11-12T14:02:11Z] trace=runtime:kvcache miss, batch_size=8, seq_len=4096
```

ops_oncall: tagging infra. Our dedicated pool for that tenant shows sustained utilization ~95% and autoscaler didn't spin up extra nodes — looks like capacity pressure + large seq lengths. :warning:

ryan_infra: I'm pulling the deploy + runtime logs now. Quick checks: which reservation size is this customer on (g4 vs a100)? sam_ae?

sam_ae: They committed to Dedicated-2 (a100 slices). Said traffic spiked after running long-context evals.

ryan_infra: Running `rdwctl logs --deployment redwood-peak-v2 --tenant acme --since 15m` shows repeated kernel OOMs and a tokenization regression trace. Example:
```
runtime:cuda memory_alloc failed, attempted 1.2GB, available 200MB
runtime:kernel error at attention_cuda: index out of bounds
```
That explains 500s. The X-Rate-Limit-Remaining header likely came from our circuit-breaker kicking in after repeated failures -> 429-ish behavior for safety.

maria_se: I can do a canary rollback to 2.1-stable (previous commit) — will restore expected kernel paths. ETA ~15m to start, ~30m to verify with Acme load. Want me to proceed?

sam_ae: Please proceed, and tell Acme ETA 30m. I'll ask them to pause ramping while we fix.

security_eng: Quick ask — while we pull logs, please avoid pasting customer PII. If any request bodies were logged, scrub before sharing. I'll run a quick scan for IPs/SSNs in logs once you provide the scrubbed set.

maria_se: Understood. Using filtered logs only. `deploy-bot` starting canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment `redwood-peak-v2 -> 2.1-stable` initiated by maria_se. Canary targets 10% traffic.

ryan_infra: I'm continuing root cause analysis. Reproduced in staging with long sequences — found commit `0f7c9e3` that changed tokenizer padding/token offsets; for certain sequences it causes KV cache pointer overflow -> OOM in attention kernel. Patch will be a one-line revert in token offset handling, compile + smoke test. Estimated patch ETA 45m if rollback not sufficient.

maria_se: Canary is routing 10% test traffic. Initial requests succeed. If green for 10m I'll promote. Monitoring latency/cpu/mem.

sam_ae: Shared an interim update with customer — told them 30m ETA and to hold traffic. They're appreciative but anxious.

ops_oncall: FYI autoscaler config: min_nodes=2 for that tenant. I'm bumping burst capacity to allow one extra node while canary completes. Will monitor cost impact.

security_eng: Scan complete on scrubbed logs — no PII found in the shared excerpts. Good to go.

ryan_infra: Canary looks stable after 6m. No more OOM traces in canary instances. Proceeding to promote to 50% then 100% over the next 20m unless we see regressions. If we fail, we'll revert and push the patch.

maria_se: Promoting now to 50%.

sam_ae: Notifying Acme of progress and ask them to resume a controlled ramp. I'll keep them on this thread.

sam_ae: Thanks team — please ping here for any new errors. If we hit any 5xx spike during promotion, prioritize rollback. :pray:
